meta.title: tezera Platform Architecture (ATP release, PRD v7)
meta.subtitle: Flutter app and Next.js portal for organisers, providers and consumers; NestJS API on AWS Lambda; PostgreSQL + DynamoDB

boundaries.label: AWS · ap-south-1 (Mumbai) · CDK + Amplify Gen 2 auth, serverless

cards.title: Where it runs: why, and alternatives
items: AWS, region ap-south-1 (Mumbai), defined as code. Why: API Gateway, the NestJS Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, the scheduler and media storage are defined in AWS CDK (infra/), and Cognito with Amplify Gen 2 (amplify/auth), all in one pnpm + Turborepo repository with stages dev and main. Everything is serverless, so nothing needs a server kept running. Alternatives: the earlier all-Amplify design (AppSync GraphQL, DynamoDB only), or a container host such as Render or Fly.io.

Amplify Hosting (web portal). Why: builds and serves the Next.js portal, including server-rendered pages, from the dev and main branches, with a preview link per pull request. Alternatives: Vercel, Netlify.

PostgreSQL host: not chosen yet. Suggestion: a hosted PostgreSQL with a connection pooler (for example Supabase or Neon) for dev, Amazon RDS later; the pooler matters because every Lambda instance opens its own connections. Local development runs PostgreSQL in Docker (port 5433).

Region ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Why: the nearest AWS region to Sri Lanka. Watch: personal data is stored outside Sri Lanka (Mumbai, plus wherever the hosted database sits), so check the PDPA's rules on cross-border transfers before launch (not checked).

Cost and access. Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS, Cognito and S3 have free monthly allowances and the hosted database has a free tier for dev; set an AWS Budgets alert before the pilot (limits not verified). Per-person IAM logins with MFA required; secrets in Parameter Store (SecureString) or Secrets Manager, never in git.

cards.title: Services and protocols: why, and alternatives
items: REST/JSON from NestJS instead of GraphQL. Why: the team writes the API as an ordinary NestJS app (runs locally on port 4000) and deploys it as one Lambda behind an API Gateway HTTP API. Routes so far: GET /me and GET /health/db. Alternatives: a container on ECS Fargate or App Runner if one Lambda starts too slowly; AppSync GraphQL (the v6 design).

API Gateway WebSocket API for live updates (chat, event status, 'Going' counts, map republishes). Why: a NestJS Lambda cannot hold sockets open. Small Lambdas save connection IDs in DynamoDB on $connect and remove them on $disconnect; DynamoDB Streams on the chat table send new messages out; NestJS sends the other updates through the API Gateway management API. Alternatives: AppSync subscriptions, a hosted service such as Ably or Pusher.

Amazon Cognito, defined with Amplify Gen 2. Why: email or phone sign-in, one group per role (attendee, organiser, vendor, freelancer, admin), pre-sign-up and post-confirmation functions. The portal and the app (Amplify Flutter auth library, proposed) sign in with Cognito directly; NestJS checks the access token with aws-jwt-verify, reads the role from the group, and makes a users row on the first request. Birthdate and the guardian tick stay in Cognito.

Firebase Cloud Messaging (push). Why: one service for Android and iOS (iOS through APNs), with a Flutter plugin, called from Lambda. Amazon Pinpoint is not used: AWS ends its support on 30 October 2026. Alternatives: Amazon SNS mobile push, OneSignal.
Amazon SES (email). Why: inside AWS and cheap per message. Watch: new accounts start in the SES sandbox; request production access before the pilot. Alternatives: Resend, Brevo.

Dialog e-SMS (sign-up codes and urgent alerts). Why: a Sri Lankan operator's gateway with sender ID masking and billing in LKR. Codes go through a Cognito custom SMS sender Lambda (proposed, not built). Watch: needs a Dialog Enterprise account and its API documentation is thin, so test early. Alternatives: Amazon SNS SMS, Notify.lk.

Amazon Bedrock with Claude (AI map draft, Could), called from NestJS or a Lambda. Why: stays inside AWS, uses IAM, no separate API key. Watch: Claude on Bedrock in ap-south-1 is not verified; it may need cross-region inference. Alternatives: the Anthropic API directly.

cards.title: Recommended stack (PRD v7)
items: One pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (Tezera-LK/tezera): apps/api (NestJS), apps/web (Next.js), amplify/ (auth only), infra/ (AWS CDK); the Flutter app goes in apps/mobile (proposed, not in the repository yet)
Mobile: Flutter (Dart) for Android and iOS; one app for all roles
Web: Next.js portal on Amplify Hosting for every role, consumers included; the admin panel is admin-only routes in the same app
API: NestJS (TypeScript) as one Lambda behind an API Gateway HTTP API, defined in CDK (infra/lib/api-stack.ts), stages dev and main
Data: PostgreSQL 16 through Prisma 6 (the schema and migrations are the only way to change tables) for core data; DynamoDB for chat, the promotion feed and WebSocket connection IDs
Jobs: an SQS queue (with a dead-letter queue) and EventBridge Scheduler trigger Lambda functions; DynamoDB Streams on the chat table drive live chat

cards.title: Venue map builder and interactive 2D map
items: Map builder on the web portal: organisers draw, move, resize, label and delete zones, stalls and pins over a background, with grid snapping, undo and a scale set from two marked points; the mobile app does quick on-the-day edits (move, rename, hide)
Three ways to start: a PNG/JPG or PDF floor plan (a Lambda turns the PDF's first page into the background image), a blank grid of a set size, or a saved venue map

Every map, however it starts, is saved in one standard, versioned map JSON: background, scale, and zones, stalls and pins as boxes or points in 0–1 coordinates with stable IDs; each publish is a new version, an earlier one can be restored, and open screens get the new version over the WebSocket API

AI draft (Could): NestJS or a Lambda sends the floor plan image to Claude on Amazon Bedrock and gets draft zones and stalls back; it opens as an editable draft, nothing publishes until the organiser checks it, and text in the image is treated as data. Claude in ap-south-1 not verified (may need cross-region inference)
Concept and code reused from Damian's own ai-studio repo (image to editable draft, click to edit, a new revision per save), adapted to this stack rather than lifted whole
Consumers tap a zone to see its stalls; each stall shows the vendor, items and prices in LKR
Search by item (e.g. 'kottu') highlights matching stalls; 'Find on map' jumps to a stall
Map JSON versions in PostgreSQL (a JSONB column, proposed), background images in S3; drawn as an overlay: a Flutter canvas in the app (proposed), SVG in Next.js
Mobile app only: keeps an opened event's map, times and announcements offline, with a 'last updated' time (Could)

cards.title: Sandboxed payments (Should)
items: Sandbox only in the ATP: PayHere test mode, no real money moves; every payment screen and receipt says 'Test payment, no real money'
Direct to the payee: each provider (and each organiser, for stall fees) connects their own PayHere merchant account; the web portal opens its hosted checkout and the app uses the PayHere Flutter SDK

Tezera never holds, splits or pays out funds. Holding or splitting money would most likely need CBSL registration as a money or value transfer service (LKR 15m capital), so this design also works for a real launch (not legal advice)
Covers booking deposits and instalments, stall fees, and cancellation fees and refunds per the booking's terms; Tezera's commission is a separate receipt line (rate proposed, not charged in the ATP)
PayHere sits behind a payment-provider interface in NestJS, so Genie Business or WEBXPAY can be added later

PayHere's notify call reaches a plain REST route on the HTTP API (POST /payments/payhere/notify, proposed); NestJS checks the signature, ignores repeats of an order ID, and writes the payment to PostgreSQL, which marks the instalment received; merchant secrets stay in AWS Secrets Manager
Card details are entered only on PayHere's page (PCI DSS SAQ A scope); a payee with no connected account is paid outside the app and the instalment is marked received by hand

cards.title: Data models (PostgreSQL via Prisma, plus DynamoDB)
items: PostgreSQL: accounts, profiles and verification
PostgreSQL: events, hiring marketplace (direct bookings, job posts, quotes, payment terms, instalments) and stalls
PostgreSQL: payments (sandbox): connected accounts, payments, refunds, receipts
PostgreSQL: reviews and ranking (rank score, badges, leaderboards)
PostgreSQL: venue maps (versioned map JSON, saved venue maps, stall items and prices)
PostgreSQL: community boards, meetups and announcements (proposed); admin verification, report queue, disputes and audit log
DynamoDB: chat messages (organiser–provider, consumer DMs, event group chats, community chats)
DynamoDB: promotion feed items (posts, likes, comments, shares) and WebSocket connection IDs

cards.title: Data design across two databases (replaces the DynamoDB-only design)
items: PostgreSQL is the main database; DynamoDB holds high-volume, key-lookup data. NestJS is the only code that writes either one (plus the WebSocket Lambdas, for connection IDs)
No foreign keys across the two: DynamoDB items store the PostgreSQL users.id as a string
Rank score: a rank_score column on profiles, indexed by category and district; recalculated in NestJS in the same transaction when a review is written or hidden, or queued (proposed)
Leaderboards: indexed queries, or a materialised view refreshed on a schedule (proposed)
Search: PostgreSQL full-text search plus pg_trgm trigram indexes, so typing mistakes still match; Algolia or Typesense only if the pilot needs them
Trending: a scheduled job scores recent feed posts and stores the top list (score proposed)
Tools: Prisma schema and migrations for every table change; PostgreSQL in Docker for local work

cards.title: Reviews and trust
items: Organiser and provider reviews unlock on a completed booking or a confirmed stall
Attendee reviews unlock from a 'Going' mark made before the event, once it ends
EventBridge Scheduler closes review windows after 14 days; NestJS recalculates the rank score when a review is written or hidden
Verification documents sit in a private S3 prefix that only admins can open, through short-lived signed links (PDPA)

cards.title: Still open
items: Shared PostgreSQL host for dev (hosted with a pooler suggested; RDS later)
How the deployed API gets the Cognito IDs for each stage, and who updates infra/lib/api-stack.ts
Flutter app not started; Dialog e-SMS custom SMS sender not built
PDPA cross-border transfer: data in Mumbai and wherever the database host sits

cards.title: Out of scope
items: Ticketing: tiers, seats, RSVP tickets, QR entry, ticket refunds
Real money: the ATP uses the PayHere sandbox only
Google Maps directions to the venue: still under discussion
Dropped in v7: AppSync / Amplify Data GraphQL, React Native + Expo, Expo Push, the separate payments Lambda function URL, the DynamoDB-only data design
